history.body: Hi, saw the Pearl ad. My partner and I are renting now and just checking whether buying around here could make sense. What should we know?

A useful first thing to know: all Pearl Residences Phase 1 homes are Type A, with 900 sq. ft., 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony. For a couple, the extra room could offer flexibility for work or guests, if that would be useful. What would make buying feel worthwhile compared with renting for you—more space, a place of your own long-term, or the monthly cost?
The monthly cost is the main thing. One of us has variable freelance income, so we’re unsure whether buying would fit without cutting into our savings.

That’s a sensible concern, especially with variable income. Using the stated RM0.18/sq.ft. maintenance fee inclusive of sinking fund, a 900 sq.ft. home works out to about RM162/month for maintenance alone; that doesn’t include the loan payment or other costs, and the latest fee should be confirmed. I’d test affordability against a lower-income month and protect your savings buffer. What total monthly housing amount would feel comfortable for both of you even in a leaner month?
RM162 is useful as one part, but I haven’t worked out a monthly ceiling yet. I’d need to compare it with the likely unit price and financing first. What starting price should I use as a reference?

The indicative reference I have is RM301,760, calculated from a RM328,000 base with an 8% rebate for a Block 1B podium-blocked Level 1–4 category, using a package snapshot dated 14 August 2026. It isn’t a confirmed current offer or an all-in unit price: parking or other applicable components may add cost, and the latest unit price and package need confirmation. It should give you a rough price anchor for your financing comparison.
That gives us a rough anchor, thanks. Since it’s an older indicative reference, we’d still need current pricing and a lender estimate before we can judge the monthly commitment.

That’s the right comparison. The RM301,760 figure was only an older indicative reference, not confirmed current pricing, so I’ll have the latest starting price and package checked. A lender can estimate repayments using your income and commitments—especially in a leaner freelance month—and you can keep the RM162 maintenance estimate separate from the loan and other costs.
Okay, please share the updated pricing when you have it. We’ll compare it with our rent and savings before deciding what to do next.

Of course—the current pricing and package check is already underway. I’ll share the verified figures once available, with any applicable costs clearly separated, so you can compare them against your rent and savings buffer.
